title: 2005 AMC 10B Problem 17
statement: Suppose that \(4^a = 5,\) \(5^b = 6,\) \(6^c = 7,\) and \(7^d = 8.\) What is \(a \cdot b \cdot c \cdot d?\)

solutions.text:
Chaining the equations, \[ \begin{aligned} 4^{abcd} &= \left(\left(\left(4^a\right)^b\right)^c\right)^d \\ &= \left(\left(5^b\right)^c\right)^d \\ &= \left(6^c\right)^d = 7^d = 8. \end{aligned} \]

Since \(8 = 4^{\frac{3}{2}},\) we conclude \(a \cdot b \cdot c \cdot d = \dfrac32.\)

Thus, B is the correct answer.
